cli.flow.absolute_path_in_a_place_field: flow {flow} has an absolute path in a place field: {fields}. A flow must not know where the repository is — the root comes from whoever launches. It is taken out with «sailor flow relocate {flow}».
cli.flow.beat_could_not_look: the beat did not run, and this is not «nothing was due»: with no last runs no schedule can be judged. {why}
cli.flow.cap_negative: a negative cap means nothing: {micros}. Zero is «it must spend nothing», «{none}» is «nobody set a limit»
cli.flow.cap_not_a_number: «{value}» is neither a number of micro-units nor the word «{none}». A million is one unit of currency: `sailor flow cap {name} 1000000` sets a cap of 1.00
cli.flow.due_could_not_look: nothing is listed as due, and this is not «nothing is»: with no last runs nothing can be judged. {why}
cli.flow.every_zero_seconds: «every 0 seconds» means nothing: a flow always due would restart the moment it finished. To take it off entirely: «{none}»
cli.flow.file_does_not_match_id: «{name}» sits in a file not named after its own `id` («{id}»), and writing it would go to «{id}.flow.json»: either a second flow would be created, or somebody else's would be rewritten. Rename the file after its `id`, or change the `id` so it matches the file name
cli.flow.file_without_the_suffix: «{name}» sits in «{file}», and writing it would go to «{name}.flow.json»: a second flow would be born instead of replacing this one. Rename the file with the «.flow.json» suffix
cli.flow.how_a_schedule_is_written: «{value}» is not a schedule. There are three shapes: «3600s» (every so many seconds since the last run), «07:30» (once a day, from that local hour), «{none}» (no schedule: it starts by hand only)
cli.flow.ledger_would_not_be_read: the ledger in {where} is there and would not be read: {error}
cli.flow.loads_but_no_source_lists_it: flow {name} loads but appears in no source: the two paths that look for flows have come apart
cli.flow.no_schedule_has_no_weight: «{none}» takes the schedule off, and a schedule that is not there has no weight: «{word}» has nowhere to go
cli.flow.no_schedule_yet_so_no_weight: «{name}» has no schedule yet, so it has no weight to keep: write it. `sailor flow schedule {name} {value} {light}` or `{heavy}`. I do not choose it: a weight that appeared by itself reads as a measurement and is not one
cli.flow.not_a_time_of_day: «{value}» is not a time of day: hours run from 00 to 23 and minutes from 00 to 59
cli.flow.runs_to_ask_again: {count} runs stopped on a step that said not yet, and are to be asked again:
cli.flow.tools_no_descriptor_declares: flow {flow} asks for tools no descriptor declares: {tools}. This is not «missing on this machine»: those names exist in no catalogue, so the flow runs nowhere until the name is corrected or a descriptor is added in ~/.config/sailor/tools.d/
cli.flow.two_files_one_name: «{name}» sits in two files — «{name}.flow.json» and «{name}.json» — and which of the two runs is decided by the order the system lists the directory in. I rewrite nothing until one is left: delete the one you do not want
cli.flow.value_mounted_into_an_executed_: flow {flow} mounts a value it did not write into an executed field: {fields}. The command is shell text and gets executed: what arrives from outside — from an engine or from another command — goes into «env», where it stays a piece of data, and the command reads it between quotes.
cli.flow.calls_without_cost: {count} calls declared no cost, and enter none of the figures above
cli.flow.cap_none_spends_freely: cap: none — this flow may spend whatever the run needs
cli.flow.cap_unchanged: flow {flow} ({origin}): the cap was already {cap}, nothing was touched
cli.flow.publish_commit_message: the flows as sailor published them
cli.flow.publish_why_a_literal_in_env: an «env» value written out; write a reference instead
cli.flow.publish_why_the_name_says_crede: a key named like a credential holds a value written out
cli.flow.publish_why_the_shape_is_a_toke: the value has the shape of a token
cli.flow.publish_refused_a_secret: refused: {file} carries a secret at step «{step}», key «{key}»: {why}. Nothing was published: a repository of flows is a public place, and a key that reaches it once is spent
cli.flow.publish_remote_already_named: these flows already push to {remembered}, and «{asked}» is another place: nothing was pushed. Two remotes named at different times means half the history sits where nobody looks. Change it with «git -C <the flows directory> remote set-url origin», where it is visible
cli.flow.no_flows_of_yours_to_publish: no source of flows is yours among {origins}: publishing takes the flows of whoever uses Sailor, and this run replaced that place with a declared folder
cli.flow.published_nothing_new: {count} flows in {dir}: nothing changed since the last publication
cli.flow.blind_and_asking_for_a_session: flow {flow} declares a step blind and asks it to continue a session: {steps}. The two say opposite things about the same step, and the run would honour the first — a step that judges its own chain's work is worth what it could not see. Take one of the two off: what a blind step must read goes in its prompt.
cli.flow.handed_without_choices: flow {flow} hands a step to a person without a closed choice to close it with: {steps}. A question in free text is not a step: give the step an «options» list, each with a «label» and the «facts» it rests on.
cli.flow.pointer_that_cannot_match: flow {flow} has a pointer that cannot match the shape its step will receive: {fields}. Where a step has several dependencies, or one declared skippable, the executor hands it an object keyed by dependency name with «with» laid over — so a pointer must start with one of those names. In «when» such a pointer makes the step skip, and a skipped step closes the run green; in a value it breaks the step at the first run with «unresolved_reference». Neither is what whoever wrote it meant.
cli.flow.commit_without_paths: flow {flow} runs `git commit` without saying what it commits: {steps}. With no paths, `git commit` commits everything already staged — and in a work tree shared with other sessions the index also holds another session's staged work, which then travels inside a commit that never mentions it. Say what the step commits: «--» followed by the paths, or «--only»/«--include» with a path.
cli.flow.does_not_load_so_not_rewritten: flow {flow} ({origin}) does not load, so it is not rewritten: {reason}
cli.flow.due_now_and_unplanned: {due} due now; {unplanned} with no schedule, which start by hand only
cli.flow.expired_back_among_the_ready: expired and put back among the ready: {steps}
cli.flow.held_deadline_not_passed: held, the deadline has not passed: {steps}
cli.flow.in_the_store: in the store: {runs} runs, of which {costed} spent something known
cli.flow.never_run_here: flow {flow} has never run on this machine
cli.flow.no_flow_by_that_name: no flow is called {flow}; the ones in sight are: {names}
cli.flow.no_run_is_waiting: no run is waiting for anybody
cli.flow.no_schedule_by_hand_only: no schedule: it starts by hand only
cli.flow.no_schedule_starts_by_hand: {none} — it starts only when somebody asks
cli.flow.no_store_here: no store in {path}: nothing has run yet
cli.flow.no_suggestion_yet: no suggestion: it takes at least {needed} costed runs, and there are {costed}. A number worked out on fewer samples is a datum invented with the face of a measurement, and whoever receives it rests a decision on it
cli.flow.no_trigger_step: flow {flow} has no trigger step: there is nowhere to put a brief
cli.flow.not_a_weight: «{word}» is not a weight: the words are «{light}» and «{heavy}»
cli.flow.not_due_last_ran: not due: last ran {minutes} minutes ago
cli.flow.partial_counts: partial: {without_tokens} calls with no declared tokens, {without_cost} with no known cost
cli.flow.past_models_all_priced: models used by past runs: all priced ({models})
cli.flow.schedule_unchanged: flow {flow} ({origin}): the trigger was already {before}, nothing was touched
cli.flow.ships_inside_the_binary: «{flow}» ships inside the binary: there is no file to rewrite. To change it, write a flow of the same name in your home or in the project — yours wins — and change that one. I will not do it for you: a flow that appeared by itself is a flow nobody knows they have
cli.flow.suggestion: suggestion: {suggested} micro ({units}) — the dearest run observed ({worst_run}) plus the dearest call observed ({dearest_call}). The second term is not a safety margin: it is the grain at which the cap can stop, because the check comes before opening a front
cli.flow.tokens_line: token: {in} in · {out} out · {read} read from cache · {written} written to cache
cli.flow.totals_not_split: totals not split out (those that declare neither side): {count}
cli.flow.trigger_input_not_an_object: the trigger input of {flow} is not an object but {other}: there is nowhere to put the text
desktop.beat.could_not_look: held: the beat could not read the ledger ({why})
desktop.beat.still_running: still running from an earlier start
cli.flow.cap_will_not_count_them: and the spend cap will not count those calls: it will stop later than it declares, or not stop at all
cli.flow.models_never_run_here: models: this flow has never run here, so there is no telling which will answer, nor whether the price list will know how to price them
cli.flow.models_store_unreadable: models: the ledger could not be read, so there is no telling which models this flow has used
cli.flow.models_the_price_list_cannot_pr:
models the price list cannot price: {models}
  their consumption is in the tokens above, their cost is not: the figure in currency is lower than the real one
cli.flow.spend_cap: spend cap: {micros} micros ({units} of equivalent cost)
cli.flow.what_the_cap_does_not_promise:
what the cap does not promise:
  - it does not reach the engines: the brake sits before opening a front, never inside a call already under way, and no engine knows the cap exists
  - a run's first front is never braked: with no call observed the width stays at the ceiling of four, because tightening on a number that does not exist would be inventing it
  - it counts only the calls that declare a cost; those that do not stay out of the sum, so the real spend is higher than the counted one
cli.command.faults: faults met while building: what happened, and the check that would prevent it
cli.command.flow: lists, checks, runs or resumes the flows declared in flows/
cli.command.inventory: lists skills, agents, commands, rules and hooks, and says which are switched off
cli.command.models: lists the model catalogue, shows or changes which one is in use
cli.command.profiles: lists, creates and switches the profiles of a known command line
cli.command.release: puts into service a binary built from HEAD, never from the working tree
cli.command.remaining: how much quota the person has already used, read from the engine rather than guessed
cli.command.run: starts a command line under its active profile, replacing this process
cli.command.session: tracks terminals: who checks in, what happens, and what is on the machine
cli.command.step: takes charge of and closes a step a flow has handed over
cli.command.terminal: runs a command line in a terminal Sailor owns, and can be typed into
cli.command.workspace: declares the project root, so a flow does not have to know it
cli.command.worktree: the trees this repository is checked out into
cli.faults.a_path_of_this_machine: the text carries an absolute path of this machine, from character {at} ({count} thing(s) found). It is true here and on no other machine, and the record is published
cli.faults.a_private_name: the text carries a name this machine declares private, from character {at} ({count} thing(s) found). It is not repeated here: this terminal can be recorded. The record is published, so the name has to go before it is written
cli.faults.written: the table is written into {file}: {count} faults
cli.faults.brought_in: brought in {count} faults from {file}; the store now holds {total}
cli.faults.no_prevention: «what_would_prevent» is missing: a fault without the check that would have stopped it is an anecdote, not work
cli.faults.no_rows_to_check: {file}: no row with six columns in it. Reporting «they agree» after reading nothing is the failure this command exists to prevent
cli.faults.no_rows_to_import: {file}: no row with six columns in it. Better to stop than to import nothing and call it done
cli.faults.only_in_the_store: {numbers} are in the store and not in the table - either unpublished work, or this checkout is older than the store
cli.faults.only_in_the_table: {numbers} are in the table and not in the store - «sailor faults import {file}» brings them in
cli.faults.recorded: recorded fault {number}: the store gave it the number
cli.faults.same_number_other_text: {numbers} have the same number and different text. The table is the register, so importing makes the store agree - but importing an older checkout overwrites newer text with older, and nothing says so afterwards
cli.faults.shape_of_a_fault: a fault is written as JSON with happened_on, what_happened, how_it_showed, what_would_prevent and status: {error}
cli.faults.still_open_out_of: {open} still open out of {total}, counted now and not copied
cli.faults.text_replaced: {numbers} already existed and their text was replaced by this file's. If this checkout is older than the store, that was a step back
cli.faults.they_agree: the store and {file} say the same thing: {count} faults
cli.faults.they_differ: the store and {file} say different things. Two readings, and this command cannot tell them apart - check which before moving anything:
cli.help.heading:
sailor <command> [options]

available commands:
cli.inventory.command_lines_looked_at: command lines looked at: {count} — the ones declared in the shipped descriptor and in ~/.config/sailor/extensions.d/. One that nobody declared was not searched, and says nothing here either way.
cli.no_such_form: «{verb}» is not a form of this command
cli.no_telling_where_i_am: there is no telling where I am: {error}
cli.value_is_another_option: «--{option}» was given «--{given}» as its value: the real value is missing
cli.not_a_form_of_this_command: «{verb}» is not a form of this command; there are {forms}
cli.faults.form.add: record a fault; the store gives it a number
cli.faults.form.render: write the table out, for whoever reads it that way
cli.faults.form.import: bring in a hand-written table, once
cli.faults.form.check: the store against the table; non-zero if they differ
cli.inventory.form.changes: what has appeared and what has gone
cli.session.form.open: records a terminal and who arrived at it
cli.session.form.event: records a fact about the session
cli.session.form.list: what is on record as tracked
cli.session.form.census: what is on the machine right now
cli.session.form.install: grafts every command line that declares how, and names those that do not
cli.session.form.uninstall: takes the graft back out, and names what it could not take out and why
cli.session.common_options:
common options: --tty <name> to say the terminal instead of deducing it,
                --store <file> to write somewhere other than beside the ledger
cli.terminal.form.run: runs a command line in a terminal Sailor owns
cli.terminal.form.press: types a line into a terminal Sailor holds
cli.terminal.form.reset: empties a running session the way its descriptor says
cli.terminal.form.mandate: leaves the work for whoever comes next
cli.terminal.form.list: which terminals can be typed into, and how full
cli.terminal.form.host: holds the window's terminals, so they outlive the window
cli.terminal.host_purpose: holds the terminals the window opened
cli.terminal.no_reset_declared: «{cli}» does not declare how a running session of it is emptied. Nobody has measured it, which is not the same as it being impossible: add `reset_context` to its descriptor rather than guessing a line here
cli.terminal.no_store: I cannot tell where the store lives
cli.terminal.no_such_descriptor: «{cli}»: no descriptor of that name is loaded
cli.terminal.not_a_token_count: «{written}» is not a number of tokens
cli.terminal.not_held: {address}: Sailor is not holding this terminal ({error})
cli.terminal.not_in_a_terminal: this is not running in a terminal: give --tty <name>
cli.terminal.nothing_counted_yet: {tty}   can be typed into, nothing counted yet
cli.terminal.nothing_to_hand_on: nothing to hand on: the mandate arrives on standard input
cli.terminal.nothing_to_run: nothing to run: give a command line after `--`
cli.terminal.which_cli: which command line is running there? give --cli <id>
cli.inventory.no_bases_declared: no work base declared: I am only looking at the home. Declare them in `work-roots` inside Sailor's home, one per line, or in `SAILOR_WORK_ROOTS` separated by colons.
cli.inventory.clock_behind_epoch: the clock is behind the epoch: {error}
cli.no_home: HOME is not set: there is no telling where to open the store
cli.inventory.no_scan_yet: the store holds no scan yet: run one with --record
cli.inventory.no_working_base: no working base declared: this count is the home's alone
cli.inventory.will_not_be_written: the inventory will not be written: {error}
cli.models.choice_not_saved: the choice was accepted and not saved: {error}
cli.profiles.access.home_does_not_move: not known: the home of «{id}» does not move with a variable ({note}), so no home other than the one in force can be questioned here
cli.profiles.access.no_recipe: not known: descriptor «{tool}» does not declare how to ask it whether it is authenticated (`login_status`) — nobody looked
cli.profiles.access.no_such_executable: not known: «{executable}» is not on this machine, or no descriptor declares it
cli.profiles.access.recipe_by_halves: not known: descriptor «{tool}» declares `login_status` by halves
cli.profiles.access.unrecognised: not known: it answered «{said}», which resembles neither of the two declared forms
cli.profiles.no_home_of_its_own: nobody established where {id} keeps its home when no variable moves it: name the directory
cli.profiles.home_not_there: {path} is not a directory on this machine: nothing was adopted
cli.profiles.adopted: profile {name} of {id} is the home already at {path}: its credentials are read there, not copied
cli.release.borrowing_the_modules: the page's modules are exactly this tree's: cloned from here instead of installing a quarter of a gigabyte again
cli.release.building_the_page: == building the page in that tree ==
cli.release.built_nothing: the build succeeded and produced no {path}
cli.release.cannot_borrow_the_modules: could not borrow the page's modules ({error}); installing them instead
cli.release.cannot_check_the_old_stamp: cannot check the old stamp with git: {error}
cli.release.cannot_read_jobs_in_progress: cannot read the jobs in progress from {path}: {error}
cli.release.cannot_retry_git_clone: cannot retry git clone without hardlinks: {error}
cli.release.checkout_failed: checking HEAD out in the clone failed
cli.release.cloning_head: == cloning HEAD ({head}) of {root} into a throwaway tree ==
cli.release.dry_run: == dry run: the binary in service was NOT replaced ==
cli.release.head_does_not_compile: HEAD does not compile: nothing was replaced and the binary in service is intact
cli.release.installing_the_modules: == installing the page's modules in that tree ==
cli.release.local_clone_failed: the local clone of HEAD failed (first: {first}; without hardlinks: {second})
cli.release.modules_would_not_install: the page's modules would not install: nothing was replaced and the binary in service is intact
cli.release.no_hardlinks: note: hardlinks for the local clone are denied; copying the git objects
cli.release.no_house_to_install_into: no house to install into: HOME is not set
cli.release.no_safety_copy:
== WARNING: the safety copy could NOT be written ==
   The binary in service is the new one, but anybody's next build can still overwrite it.
cli.release.no_stamp_written: == WARNING: the stamp could NOT be written ==
cli.release.nothing_to_do: == nothing to do: the binary in service already matches HEAD ({head}) ==
cli.release.page_does_not_build: the page does not build: nothing was replaced and the binary in service is intact
cli.release.cannot_read_what_was_built: cannot read {path} back to look for the page inside it: {error}
cli.release.page_has_no_files: the page was built and {path} holds no file to embed: there was nothing to put inside the binary
cli.release.page_is_not_inside: the binary that was built does not carry the page: {missing} of {of} files are not in it, starting with «{first}». A window like that opens blank. Nothing was replaced
cli.release.partial_clone_stuck: the local clone failed and the partial clone {path} cannot be removed: {error}
cli.release.postponed_another_job:
release postponed: the service has started another job; the new binary and the stamp are in place, but the service is still running the old one.
   When that job ends, close the release with: launchctl kickstart -k {domain}
cli.release.postponed_still_working: release postponed: the service is still working; nothing was replaced
cli.release.receipt_with_no_pid: warning: receipt with no pid '{name}' (does not block the release)
cli.release.running_the_suite: == running the whole suite of {manifest} on HEAD ==
cli.release.service_is_working: waiting: the service is working on '{task}' with pid {pid}
cli.release.service_still_on_the_old_one:
the binary is in place, but the service is still running the old one ({why}).
   To close the gap run: launchctl kickstart -k {domain}
cli.release.stamp_names_the_wrong_commit:
{stamp} names {old}; the binary in service is {head}.
   Whoever reads it will name the wrong commit ({error}).
   Write this exact line by hand in {stamp}:
cli.release.suite_is_red:
the suite is red on HEAD: nothing was replaced and the binary in service is intact.
   Green commits apart do not add up to a green whole: this is that case.
   If the binary in service is broken and waiting costs more, run again with --skip-tests.
cli.release.tests_not_run:
== {count} test(s) NOT RUN (not failed) ==
   Green here does not mean tested there: the sandbox denied what they asked for.
cli.release.tests_skipped: == TESTS SKIPPED (--skip-tests): this release was NOT tested ==
cli.release.the_name_finds_another_one:
WARNING: typing «{name}» still runs {first}, which is not the copy just put in service.
   Anything that looks the name up — the window included — goes on running that one, so this release is not finished: replace it with {path}, or put that directory first on the search path.
cli.release.the_name_finds_nothing: note: «{name}» is on no search path, so nothing that looks it up will find what was just put in service
cli.release.uncommitted_stay_out: note: {count} uncommitted file(s) under {parts} stay out of service, by construction
cli.release.unknown_target: unknown target '{target}'; the targets available are: {targets}
cli.release.which_commit_is_unknown:
which commit produced the binary in service is not known.
   That is expected the first time only; from now on the answer is written in {stamp}.
cli.remaining.no_channel: no engine on this machine declares a channel to read its quota from: nothing to ask
cli.remaining.no_channel_declared: {engine} · nobody asked: its descriptor declares no channel to read the quota from. This is «nobody looked», not «no quota»
cli.remaining.no_window: no quota window declared: the channel answered with no measurements
cli.remaining.whose_quota: the PERSON's quota, not a run's: it counts every session, including the ones outside Sailor
cli.run.active_profile_gone: the active profile '{profile}' for {id} is no longer in the state
cli.run.home_mechanism_unknown: {cli}: how it moves its home directory is not known yet ({note}); sailor run refuses to guess
cli.run.link_points_elsewhere: {link} points at {actual}, but the active profile wants {wanted}: the state and the disk have come apart. Run 'sailor profiles switch' again for that command line before launching it
cli.run.link_unreadable: cannot read the link {link}: {error}. Without it there is no telling which identity it would start under
cli.run.no_active_profile: no active profile for {cli}: use 'sailor profiles switch {id} <name>' before starting it
cli.session.detached: {tty} is detached: it stays so for whoever arrives here later
cli.session.moments_without_an_event: {tool}: {moments} have no event on this command line, so they are not grafted. Not filled with the nearest one: a welcome on the wrong event arrives at every turn instead of once
cli.session.no_process_has_a_terminal: no process has a terminal, and asking was possible
cli.session.no_terminal_anywhere: there is no telling which terminal this process runs on: none of its three descriptors is a tty, and no process above it on the parent chain has one either. Say it with --tty <name>
cli.session.no_typed_words: {tool}: no words a user types, so the welcome promises none
cli.session.nothing_grafted: nothing was grafted anywhere. That is a statement, not a silence: read the lines above for which command line refused and why
cli.session.ledger_did_not_open: the ledger did not open ({why}), so this greeting cannot say whether anything is waiting: that is «I could not look», not «nothing is open».
cli.session.not_announced: you were not announced to the other agents ({why}), so the crew survey will not show this terminal: it will read as an empty tree, not as a terminal that could not speak.
cli.session.others_in_this_tree: {count} other terminal(s) are open in this tree, by the register: {who}. Uncommitted work here may be theirs, and a measurement taken over the working tree measures theirs too — so read what a clean HEAD says before seeding any ratchet, and before calling the tree green. The register does not know what is alive: a terminal killed without closing stays in this list.
cli.session.runs_to_ask_again: {count} run(s) stopped on a step that answered «not yet»: {which}. They come back only when somebody runs them again: `sailor flow resume {first}`.
cli.session.runs_waiting_for_a_person: {count} run(s) of the ledger are waiting for a person to take them up: {which}. Nothing takes them on its own — `sailor flow resume {first}` does.
cli.session.root_not_an_object: {file}: the root is not an object
cli.session.word_body: Run `sailor session {verb}` and report in one line what it answered. Do nothing else.
cli.session.word_off: Detach this terminal from Sailor: it stops being tracked, and so do the sessions opened here afterwards.
cli.session.word_on: Attach this terminal to Sailor again, if it had been detached.
cli.session.census_refused: I DO NOT KNOW: I was not allowed to look at the machine ({refusal}). This is not «no terminal»
cli.session.a_line_that_did_not_say: a command line that did not say
cli.session.declares_no_hooks: {tool}: left alone — it does not declare how it is told a session started, so Sailor has never written anything for it
cli.session.form_not_listed: «{form}» reads the ledger but is not in NEEDS_THE_STORE: that is a defect of session_cmd.rs, not of the line you typed
cli.session.had_no_open_row: {tty} had no open row: the fact is recorded all the same
cli.session.home_below_yours: {tool}: «{variable}» is not set here, so the home below yours was grafted. A session started where it IS set reads another file and will not see these hooks
cli.session.home_the_variable_names: {tool}: «{variable}» is set here to {root}, so that is the home grafted. A session started where it says something else reads another file and will not see these hooks
cli.session.no_settings_address: {tool}: its settings file has no address
cli.session.none_checked_in: no terminal has checked in yet
cli.session.nothing_to_graft: {tool}: declares a hooks file and no event names, so there is nothing to graft into it
cli.session.settings_without_tool: «--settings» says where to write and not for whom: name the command line with «--tool <id>» too. Without it, one file would be handed to whichever line the code happened to know, which is the coupling this command just had taken out of it
cli.session.toml_already_a_plain_table: «{key}» is already a plain table here, and appending an array of tables of that name would not parse: nothing was written
cli.session.toml_ends_inside_a_value: the file ends inside a value, so this reader will not append to it: nothing was written
cli.session.toml_header_unreadable: line {line}: a table header this reader cannot make sense of, so nothing was appended: {text}
cli.session.toml_is_an_array_of_tables: «{key}» is an array of tables here, and a table appended at the end would join its last entry rather than the whole: nothing was written
cli.session.toml_key_of_the_same_name: «{table}» already holds «{key}» as a key of its own, and appending a table of that name would not parse: nothing was written
cli.session.toml_no_key: no key is declared for the hooks, so there is nowhere to put them and nothing was written
cli.session.toml_root_assigns_the_key: the root of the file already assigns «{key}» as a key, so a table of that name cannot be opened at the end: nothing was written
cli.session.toml_used_as_a_table: «{table}» is already used as a table here, so «{key}» is not free at the end of the file: nothing was written
cli.session.uninstall.empty_object_left: {file} now holds an empty object: Sailor does not delete a file it cannot be sure it created
cli.session.uninstall.format_not_taken_b: {tool}: its hooks live in {file}, a format the graft writes and this inverse cannot take back out yet — so anything of ours in there is STILL THERE. Nothing was touched: look in that file by hand
cli.session.uninstall.no_file: nothing of ours: {file} is not there
cli.session.uninstall.no_hooks: nothing of ours: {file} holds no hooks
cli.session.uninstall.not_an_array: «{event}» is not an array in {file}, so it was not read: anything of ours under it is still there
cli.session.uninstall.nothing_read: no settings file was read at all. That is a statement, not a silence: read the lines above for which command line refused and why
cli.session.uninstall.word_not_ours: /{word} stays: {file} is not the file Sailor writes
cli.session.rules: The rules of this tree are written in {files}: read them before changing anything here.
cli.session.welcome:
You are connected to Sailor.
terminal {tty} · tree {worktree}
This terminal is tracked: Sailor knows you exist, which tree you work in, and when you will need to hand on.
To detach it: /sailor-off
cli.step.author_would_judge: «{holder}» has already closed {dependency}, which {step_id} depends on: whoever creates does not judge. Use another name, or declare `"same_holder_ok": true` in the step if the flow really wants the same hand
cli.step.already_open: step {step_id} is open: somebody is already running it, and it was not handed over. Close it first, or resume the run with `sailor flow resume {run_id}`
cli.step.cannot_work_out_what_is_ready: cannot work out what is ready: {error}
cli.step.flow_does_not_load: flow {flow} ({origin}) of run {run_id} does not load: {reason}
cli.step.no_such_run: no run is called {run_id} in this store
cli.step.not_waiting: step {step_id} is not waiting but {outcome}: there is no handover to take charge of
cli.step.ready_now: ready now: {steps}. Resume with: sailor flow resume {run_id}
cli.step.run_complete: the run is complete: nothing is left to do
cli.step.flow_declares_no_such_step: flow {flow} declares no step {step_id}: the ledger and the file have come apart
cli.step.flow_no_longer_found: flow {flow} of run {run_id} is no longer to be found: it was on this machine when the run started
cli.step.held_by_the_engine: step {step_id} is held by process {pid}: it was handed to nobody, the engine is running it. If that process died, use `sailor flow resume {run_id}`
cli.step.none_open: run {run_id} has no step {step_id} open: take it on with `sailor step open` before closing it
cli.step.outcome_not_declarable: «--outcome {outcome}» is not an outcome a person can declare: the values are `went` and `broke`
cli.step.output_breaks_the_schema: the declared output does not meet step {step_id}'s schema: {error}. The step was not closed — a malformed output accepted here would kill the run later on, and the blame would fall on another step
cli.step.run_declares_no_flow: run {run_id} does not declare which flow it comes from: without it there is no telling which graph to load
cli.step.self_declared_turns: {turns} self-declared turns, at no cost: they join the calls the total does not know about, and from now on this run's spend is an «at least»
cli.step.not_yet: not yet: {steps}. Ready again in {seconds} s. Ask again with: sailor flow resume {run_id}
cli.step.waiting_for_someone: waiting for someone: {steps}. Take the work with: sailor step open --run {run_id} --step <step> --as <who>
cli.step.would_close_without_output: step {step_id} would close with no output, but {dependents} depends on it and demands a typed one: the run would stop there. Declare it with `--output-file <file>`
cli.workspace.already_declared: {file} is already there: this command does not overwrite a declaration, because someone may have written into it by hand
cli.workspace.no_house_to_read: no house to read: HOME is not set
cli.workspace.none_known: no project has been opened yet: run «sailor workspace init» inside one
run.failure.ambiguous_reference: this reference is not alone in its object
run.failure.answer_off_shape: the answer is not in the declared shape
run.failure.answer_too_large: the command printed more than an answer can hold — it was refused, not cut short
run.failure.check_timed_out: the check went past its time limit
run.failure.child_run_not_recorded: the child run could not be recorded in the store
run.failure.clock_before_epoch: the machine's clock reads a time before 1970 — the subflow never opened
run.failure.clock_broke: the machine's clock would not say the time
run.failure.empty_signal: the signal arrived with nothing in it
run.failure.engine_exhausted: the engine ran out of its quota — it did not break
run.failure.engine_exit_error: the engine exited with an error
run.failure.engine_timed_out: the engine went past its time limit
run.failure.history_unreadable: the run history could not be read — an empty one would say so
run.failure.invalid_input: the step's inputs are not in the expected shape
run.failure.invalid_recovered_output: the recovered result is not in the declared shape — the work was done
run.failure.invalid_reference: the reference is written wrong — nothing was even looked up
run.failure.invalid_subflow: the flow is there, but it could not be read — the name is not what is wrong
run.failure.invalid_subflow_call: the step's call to another flow is not in the expected shape
run.failure.listening_not_built: this trigger source cannot listen yet
run.failure.mandate_not_taken: the mandate was read but could not be taken away, so it was not handed on
run.failure.no_compensation: this kind of step claims it can undo its own effect, and it cannot
run.failure.no_ledger: there is nowhere to record the subflow — so it did not start
run.failure.no_parent_run: there is no run in progress — a subflow only exists inside one
run.failure.no_parent_step: no step is in progress — there would be nothing to attribute the child run to
run.failure.no_preflight: no check ties the server's answer to the directory this step is about
run.failure.no_store: nobody knows where the store lives
run.failure.no_tool_resolver: nobody knows where to find that tool
run.failure.no_usable_engine: none of the engines the step asks for could work
run.failure.nobody_keeps_the_time: this trigger is fired by the clock, and the clock is kept on the flow's schedule, not on this source
run.failure.reset_not_declared: nobody has written down how a session of that command line is emptied
run.failure.shape_not_in_prompt: the shape demanded was never asked of the engine
run.failure.store_refused: the store did not take the write
run.failure.store_unreadable: the store did not answer — this is not a missing entry
run.failure.subflow_broke: the subflow's run broke off before it could say how it ended
run.failure.subflow_cap_reached: the subflow stopped at its spending cap — it did not break
run.failure.subflow_cycle: a flow ends up calling itself, if not directly then through the ones it calls
run.failure.subflow_failed: a step inside the subflow failed and had no attempts left
run.failure.subflow_incomplete: the subflow's run came back with steps still open — none of them failed
run.failure.subflow_stopped: a step of the subflow was stopped and left that way — it did not fail
run.failure.subflow_too_deep: too many flows are stacked one inside another — this is the depth limit, not a loop
run.failure.subflow_unknown_state: the subflow's run ended in a state this version has no name for
run.failure.subflow_unreadable: the store could not be read — the fault is not in the flow
run.failure.terminal_not_held: Sailor is not holding that terminal
run.failure.tool_unavailable: that tool is not on this machine
run.failure.patch_refused: the patch was not applied: it names a file nobody assented to, or one behind the wall no assent opens
run.failure.tree_not_cut: the step asked for a tree of its own and git could not cut it, so it was not run in the shared one
run.failure.unjoinable_reference: only text can be joined, and one of the pieces is not text
run.failure.unknown_action: the step calls for an action nobody here knows
run.failure.unknown_command_line: no descriptor is loaded for that command line — it may be missing, switched off, or broken
run.failure.unknown_step: the flow being resumed has no step by that name
run.failure.unknown_subflow: no flow by that name, in any of the places flows are looked for
run.failure.unresolved_reference: the step asks for a value its input does not contain
run.failure.work_is_shared: another agent has already announced this working tree, and the step asked to stop when that happens
cli.command.ratchet: measures the judges with a seed on a clean HEAD with only this tree's changes laid over
cli.ratchet.says: runs every seeded judge on a clean copy of HEAD plus the files this tree changed, and prints the seeds to write
cli.ratchet.not_a_repository: the sources are not a git repository
cli.ratchet.archive_failed: git archive HEAD did not produce a tree
cli.ratchet.no_judge: no judge carries a seed here
cli.ratchet.measuring: measuring {judges} judge(s) on a clean HEAD, {laid_over} changed file(s) laid over
cli.ratchet.all_green: every seed holds on HEAD with these changes
cli.ratchet.some_red: a seed does not hold: the lines above say what to write
cli.release.suite_already_green: the suite already passed on this tree ({tree}): not run again
cli.release.suite_not_remembered: the suite passed but {memo} could not be written ({error}): the next release runs it again
cli.release.not_pushed: not pushed, the remote is behind: {line}
run.failure.search_refused: the search was refused — a word is needed, or the flows could not be ranked
